maria: heads up — onboarding Mixtral-8B-slim from HF. After conversion to safetensors we see a 20-30% tail-latency regression on p99. profile attached below (short).

ajay: can you paste the hf config and the convert command?

maria: convert used `scripts/convert_to_safetensors.py --model mixtral-8b --out mixtral-8b.safetensors`
HF config excerpt:
```
architectures: ["MixtralForCausalLM"]
num_attention_heads: 32
hidden_size: 4096
rotary_pct: 0.25
rope_scaling: null
```
logs: `ERROR runtime: kv_cache shape mismatch: (batch=1, nheads=32, head_dim=128) vs expected head_dim=160`

liam: that mismatch screams head_dim mismatch between model metadata and runtime heuristics. Did the converter drop or mis-encode `head_dim` or `num_key_value_heads`?

maria: hfmeta in safetensors shows `num_key_value_heads` missing. HF parse fell back to inferring from shape which gave 32*128. runtime expects 32*160 (we use 160 head dim for mixtral variant).

olga: interesting — our kernel selection picks different matmul kernels when head_dim==160 vs 128 which explains perf cliff. If runtime falls into the 128 path it ends up using a generic tiled kernel with worse perf and different KV packing -> extra memcpy.

ajay: quick triage plan:
- detect missing `num_key_value_heads` on HF parse and fail hard (for now)
- add a conversion assert to ensure safetensors metadata has `head_dim` and `num_kv_heads`
- re-run profiling with forced kernel selection to validate perf delta

maria: did a forced kernel run — set `INFERENCE_KERNEL_HINT=mixtral_fast_160` on node, reloaded model, p99 back to baseline. So kernel choice is the immediate cause. But why did converter produce 128? converter.py snippet: `head_dim = weights['query.weight'].shape[1] // num_heads` — if num_kv_heads missing defaulted to num_heads -> wrong division.

liam: that default behavior is brittle. Also batching heuristics: I noticed batcher oscillation logs around the same time — small requests fell into per-token batching which forces prefetch stride 8 and triggers extra KV evictions when head_dim mismatches. That could amplify p99.

maria: stacktrace snippet:
```
[profiler] kernel: matmul_tiled_generic (runtime choose)
[cache] evict index 0 due to stride mismatch. prev_stride=16 new_stride=8
[batcher] adaptive_window shrank -> flush
```

ajay: actionable items (short):
1) converter: fail if `num_key_value_heads` or `head_dim` absent in safetensors metadata.
2) hn: add HF-parse lint step in onboarding job that emits `ERROR` and stops rollout.
3) runtime: make kernel selection log more explicit and fall back to a safe fast-path that doesn't degrade p99 too much (temporary).
4) batcher: detect frequent kernel path flips for a model and hold window to avoid thrash.

olga: I'll file a quick PR for runtime logging and a backoff in the batcher heuristic. maria can you attach the safetensors metadata blob and converter command in the onboarding ticket? (cc @deploy-bot)

maria: done — uploaded metadata + minimal repro to https://internal/redwood/onboard/MIxtral-8B-243. Repro script: `python tools/repro_kv_mismatch.py --model-path ./mixtral-8b.safetensors --batch 1 --seq 1024`

deploy-bot: Canary deploy of converter-fix branch `fix/safetensors-metadata` scheduled to 2 nodes at 2026-05-02T15:30:00Z :eyes:

liam: one more note — roPE scaling: our defaults expect rope_scaling==null -> native. Some Mixtral variants use scale factor that changes effective head_dim in attention ops (we sometimes implement fused scaling). Add explicit check for `rope_scaling` and error if present but not supported by the runtime variant.

maria: agreed. I'll update onboarding checklist: metadata presence, rope_scaling sanity, explicit head_dim vs num_kv_heads parity, conversion assert.

olga: PR for batcher backoff in review: #3021. small perf test shows p99 improvement from 1.32s -> 0.96s on canary when kernel hint stable.

maria: thanks all — keeping this thread as single-source for the ticket. Will follow up with regression post-mortem once canary finishes. :thumbsup:
